executive_summary: Your RED status is driven entirely by peer-level geopolitical shocks, not supplier financial health or macro instability. Four suppliers cluster around US-China trade friction and Taiwan risk (Huizhou BYD, Smoore, EVE Energy, IP Sun, Porton), two around South Asian tensions (ITC in India, Tae Young in South Korea), one around Russia-NATO proximity (Stora Enso), and one around African infrastructure stress (Sappi). The immediate priority is the China cluster—those four suppliers account for critical EMS and high-BAT-exposure battery categories that feed your core product architecture; any sudden Taiwan escalation, export control tightening, or shipping disruption would cascade across multiple product lines simultaneously. Stora Enso and Sappi present slower-burn risks tied to regional stability rather than acute trade events, so they warrant contingency planning but aren't actionable this week. ITC's high nicotine BAT exposure paired with India-Pakistan border volatility deserves a secondary review, but geopolitical incidents there typically announce themselves with warning. Start by identifying which of the four China-exposed suppliers have viable alternatives in Vietnam, Indonesia, or allied markets; if not, you need dual-sourcing conversations this quarter.
